1. Seed coat (covering)

What are seeds

Is a tomato a fruit or a vegetable?
• In 1893 the U.S. Supreme Court 
decision
• Nix v. Hedden
• Nix was a fruit importer
• Hedden was a customs collector
• Vegetables required a 10% tariff, 
fruits were tax-free

vegetable.  Fruits are eaten as dessert”

Fig Wasp Pollinators
• Figs are pollinated by small wasps
• Female wasps enter the syconium 
through the ostiole
• Wings and antennae are 
stripped off

the syconium where she was 
born
• She pollinates, lays eggs in 
flowers, then dies

Fig Wasp Pollinators
• Wingless males emerge from the 
flowers first, and mate with the 
females while they’re still in the 
flowers

open, then die
• Newly emerged, fertilized 
females collect pollen
• Exit the syconium and fly to a 
new one
• Pollen may be spread over 100 km2

Water is the most abundant resource on the planet, 
yet most limiting resource for terrestrial plants

“The Pulse of the Planet”

• Short-Distance Transport
• Diffusion/Osmosis (cell to cell)
• VERY Slow process
• Less efficient over long distances
• Long-Distance Transport
• Requires specialized cell 
types/tissues
• Fast process
• More efficient over long distances

• Adhesion - sticks to other

Water moves from roots to xylem

• Plasmolysis -cells lose water and become “flaccid”

in poison. You observe that after a few

leaves fall off, the poison stops moving up

Leaves can lose up to 100% of their water in 1 hour.  Plants retain

Evaporation and Transpiration

• Occurs when stomata are 
open
• Potassium ions (K+) pumped 
into guard cells -> vacuoles 
swell with water
• Differences in cell wall 
thickness of the guard cells 
results in deformation, 
opening a gap between them 
-> opening the stomate
• Stomata close when K+ is 
pumped out of guard cells -> 
vacuoles shrink

damage than late wood (tracheids)

one fails, all fail)
